newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 29.

text.p: Murder hunt for NZ mother: Queensland's homicide squad has started a murder hunt after the disappearance of Surekha Engledow, a Fiji Indian woman from Nelson, who went missing while on a family camping holiday between Brisbane and Cairns in May last year. Page 1.
Fire Service too hasty with cuts, says Elder: Internal Affairs Minister Jack Elder has questioned whether the Fire Service is being too hasty in considering cuts to firefighter numbers. Page 1.

Postal vote to decide on Crown offer: An NZ$40 million Crown offer of settlement in the Whakatohea tribal land claim had not been rejected just because 174 people were against it, claims manager Claude Edwards said on Monday. Page 2.

Diving dollar may force Brash to make statement: Reserve Bank governor Don Brash returned from a meeting of Asian central bankers Shanghai on Monday afternoon, just in time to see the dollar crash through the floor. Page 17.
Smog package may hit poor: A double-edged sword for Christchurch's poor and elderly -- that is the welfare agency view of the planed open-fire and non-complying woodburner ban. Page 1.

PM leads MPs' party to funeral: Prime Minister Jim Bolger will be one of at least 16 MPs who will attend the funeral today of Maori leader Matiu Rata at his birthplace of Te Hapua, in the Far North. Page 6.

INL says decision on Sky still some way off: A conclusion to Independent Newspapers Ltd negotiations to buy a stake in Sky Network Television will be later than indicated, according to INL's general manager, Rick Neville. Page 31.
PNG on edge as rebel set free: Papua New Guinea was tense on Monday night after the forging of a fragile truce between rebellious troops and the infant government of Prime Minister Bill Skate.
Tri-Nations still to be won: The Bledisloe Cup is won but the Tri-Nations isn't, wary All Blacks coach John Hart says
